allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory gives scaffolding its operating logic by explaining why chunking and staged support reduce overload during learning.
allies.source_quote: Scaffolding is the implementation mechanism for respecting the limitations described by Cognitive Load Theory.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'This is the most crucial ally. Scaffolding is essentially the practical application of CLT' — reduces cognitive load by breaking complex material into manageable chunks.
allies.activation_condition: When complex material must be broken into incremental chunks to prevent working memory overload during learning or problem-solving.

allies.rationale_text: Boundaries help scaffolding define what belongs inside the current learning frame so attention stays on the next useful increment.
allies.source_quote: Scaffolding provides an essential structure that establishes boundaries, helping decision-makers focus on what is inside the frame.
allies.affinity_rationale: Moderate: scaffolding provides structural boundaries that define the learning or problem-solving path. Not directly in canonical allies.
allies.activation_condition: When clear boundaries define the scope and sequence of scaffolded steps to prevent scope creep during structured learning.

antagonists.rationale_text: System-1 undermines scaffolding by producing snap judgments and substitution bias that bypass the deliberate, structured sequencing scaffolding requires.
antagonists.source_quote: Scaffolding, as a deliberate, structured process, requires the use of slow thinking (System 2). It counters the tendency of System 1 (instinctual, fast thinking) to produce snap judgments or substitution bias, where a simple, familiar model is used instead of understanding the more complicated reality.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Moderate: scaffolding aims to overcome System 1's preference for shortcuts by imposing structured, deliberate steps. Canonical antagonists focus on Curse of Knowledge and Maslow's Hammer.
antagonists.activation_condition: When the brain's preference for fast, automatic processing resists the deliberate, structured progression that scaffolding requires.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Scaffolding conflicts with desirable-difficulties when load reduction removes the productive challenge needed for durable learning transfer.
structured_tensions.source_quote: scaffolding vs desirable-difficulties: scaffolding conflicts with desirable-difficulties (desirable difficulties) when desirable Difficulties emphasizes challenging learning conditions, contrasting with Scaffolding's focus on reducing cognitive load.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Scaffolding conflicts with confirmation-bias when the support design reflects the teacher's assumptions instead of diagnosed learner needs.
structured_tensions.source_quote: scaffolding vs confirmation-bias: scaffolding conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when scaffold design reflects the instructor's beliefs about what learners need rather than evidence-based diagnosis of actual knowledge gaps.

curation_notes.summary: Layer 1+2 enrichment complete. cognitive-load-theory at 0.95 ('most crucial ally, practical application of CLT'). boundaries at 0.80. system-1 antagonist at 0.80. Canonical also lists feynman-technique and blooms-taxonomy as allies.
donor_drops: Did not preserve broader pedagogy relation sprawl beyond the cleanest current-vocabulary support and tension links.
open_questions: Blooms-taxonomy is source-real as an ally, but the first-order surface is cleaner around cognitive-load-theory and boundaries.

SPARSE_ALLY_RECOVERY: 2 curated allies. Canonical allies include feynman-technique ('embedded within' scaffolding framework), blooms-taxonomy (structures learning journey hierarchically), first-principles-thinking (methodical decomposition path).
